docs.title: Install CB POS on Windows
docs.summary: Complete guide to downloading, system requirements, and installing CB POS on Windows 10 or 11.
docs.body_md:
# Install CB POS on Windows

CB POS is a standalone desktop Point of Sale application designed specifically for Sri Lankan retail businesses [A2]. It runs locally on your PC, is completely offline-first, and never requires an ongoing internet connection to bill customers [A2][A8].

## System Requirements

Before running the setup wizard, ensure your computer meets the minimum specifications:

- **Operating System:** Windows 10 (64-bit, version 1809 or higher) or Windows 11 [A2]. *Note: Legacy Windows 7, 8, and 8.1 are blocked by the installer [A2].*
- **Processor (CPU):** Dual-core 1.6 GHz or faster (Intel Core i3 / AMD Ryzen 3 or higher recommended) [A2].
- **Memory (RAM):** 4 GB minimum (8 GB strongly recommended for retail shops with more than 5,000 inventory items) [A2].
- **Storage:** 500 MB free hard drive space for software installation and local SQLite database storage [A2][G1].
- **Display Resolution:** 1024 × 768 pixels minimum (1366 × 768 or 1920 × 1080 Full HD recommended for optimal cashier counter layout) [A2].
- **Peripherals (Optional):** USB thermal receipt printer (58mm or 80mm) [E1], standard USB barcode scanner [E4], and electronic cash drawer with RJ12 trigger cable [E4].

## Installation Steps

:::step{title="Download the official installer"}
Download the setup executable `CBPOSSetup-1.3.0.exe` directly from the official Ceylon Byte website (`https://ceybyte.com`) or from our verified GitHub Releases repository [A3][A6].
:::

:::step{title="Run the setup wizard with Administrator rights"}
Double-click the downloaded installer. Because CB POS installs system-wide into your program files directory (`C:\Program Files\CB POS`), Windows User Account Control (UAC) will prompt for administrator permission [A4]. Click **Yes** to continue.
:::

:::step{title="Choose optional desktop shortcuts"}
The Inno Setup wizard allows you to select whether to create a Desktop icon and whether to automatically launch CB POS whenever Windows starts up [A3]. We recommend checking both options for dedicated cashier checkout terminals [A3].
:::

:::step{title="Complete setup and first launch"}
Click **Install**. The setup copies bundled Python runtime dependencies and application binaries in under two minutes [A1][A3]. When finished, leave "Launch CB POS" checked and click **Finish** [A3].
:::

:::tip
**Where is your store data saved?**
While the program executable is installed in `C:\Program Files\CB POS`, your private store database (`cbpos.db`), receipt logs, and configuration files live separately in your Windows user profile at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CB POS` [A4][G1]. When you install future updates, the installer automatically detects and preserves your existing database and business records [A4].
:::

## Unattended Deployment for POS Technicians

For IT technicians and POS service providers deploying CB POS across multiple grocery stores or branches, the installer supports Inno Setup silent switches [A4]:

```powershell
# Silent install with standard progress bar
.\CBPOSSetup-1.3.0.exe /SILENT

# Completely quiet install without UI dialogs
.\CBPOSSetup-1.3.0.exe /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES
```

Silent installations suppress the post-installation application launch so you can configure hardware drivers and peripherals first [A4].

docs.title: වින්ඩෝස් මත CB POS ස්ථාපනය කිරීම
docs.summary: වින්ඩෝස් 10 හෝ 11 මත CB POS බාගත කර ස්ථාපනය කිරීම සඳහා පියවරෙන් පියවර මාර්ගෝපදේශය.
docs.body_md:
# වින්ඩෝස් මත CB POS ස්ථාපනය කිරීම

CB POS යනු ශ්‍රී ලංකාවේ සිල්ලර වෙළඳසැල් සඳහාම නිර්මාණය කරන ලද නොමිලේ ලබාදෙන පරිගණක මෘදුකාංගයකි [A2]. එය ඔබගේ පරිගණකයේම ක්‍රියාත්මක වන අතර බිල්පත් නිකුත් කිරීම සඳහා අන්තර්ජාල සම්බන්ධතාවක් අවශ්‍ය නොවේ [A2][A8].

## පද්ධති අවශ්‍යතා

ස්ථාපනය කිරීමට පෙර ඔබගේ පරිගණකය පහත අවශ්‍යතා සපුරාලන්නේදැයි පරීක්ෂා කරන්න:

- **මෙහෙයුම් පද්ධතිය:** වින්ඩෝස් 10 (64-bit, අනුවාදය 1809 හෝ ඊට පසු) හෝ වින්ඩෝස් 11 [A2]. *(පැරණි Windows 7 සහ 8.1 සඳහා සහය නොදක්වයි [A2]).*
- **මතකය (RAM):** අවම වශයෙන් 4 GB (විශාල භාණ්ඩ ප්‍රමාණයක් ඇති වෙළඳසැල් සඳහා 8 GB නිර්දේශ කෙරේ) [A2].
- **දෘඪ තැටි ඉඩ:** මෘදුකාංගය සහ දත්ත ගබඩාව සඳහා 500 MB නිදහස් ඉඩ [A2][G1].
- **තිර විභේදනය:** අවම වශයෙන් 1024 × 768 පික්සල් [A2].

## ස්ථාපන පියවර

:::step{title="ස්ථාපන ගොනුව බාගත කරන්න"}
නිල Ceylon Byte වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් (`https://ceybyte.com`) `CBPOSSetup-1.3.0.exe` ගොනුව බාගත කරන්න [A3].
:::

:::step{title="ස්ථාපකය ක්‍රියාත්මක කරන්න"}
බාගත කළ ගොනුව මත double-click කරන්න. පරිපාලක (Administrator) අවසර ඉල්ලා සිටින විට **Yes** තෝරන්න [A4].
:::

:::step{title="කෙටිමං තෝරන්න"}
ඩෙස්ක්ටොප් එකේ කෙටිමඟක් (Desktop shortcut) සහ පරිගණකය ආරම්භ වන විටම CB POS ආරම්භ කිරීමේ විකල්පය තෝරා **Next** ක්ලික් කරන්න [A3].
:::

:::step{title="ස්ථාපනය අවසන් කරන්න"}
මිනිත්තු දෙකකට අඩු කාලයකින් මෘදුකාංගය ස්ථාපනය වී අවසන් වේ. ඉන්පසු **Finish** ක්ලික් කර මෘදුකාංගය විවෘත කරන්න [A3].
:::

:::tip
ඔබගේ සියලුම බිල්පත් සහ තොග දත්ත `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CB POS` හි සුරක්ෂිතව පවතින අතර, ඉදිරි නව අනුවාද ස්ථාපනය කිරීමේදී පැරණි දත්ත ස්වයංක්‍රීයව ආරක්ෂා වේ [A4][G1].
:::

docs.title: விண்டோஸில் CB POS ஐ நிறுவுதல்
docs.summary: விண்டோஸ் 10 அல்லது 11 இல் CB POS ஐப் பதிவிறக்கி நிறுவுவதற்கான முழுமையான வழிகாட்டி.
docs.body_md:
# விண்டோஸில் CB POS ஐ நிறுவுதல்

CB POS என்பது இலங்கையின் சில்லறை வணிகங்களுக்காக வடிவமைக்கப்பட்ட ஒரு இலவச கணினி மென்பொருளாகும் [A2]. இது உங்கள் கணினியில் முழுமையாக ஆஃப்லைனில் இயங்குகிறது, பில்களை வழங்க இணைய இணைப்பு தேவையில்லை [A2][A8].

## கணினி தேவைகள்

நிறுவுவதற்கு முன் உங்கள் கணினி பின்வரும் தேவைகளைப் பூர்த்தி செய்கிறதா என்பதைச் சரிபார்க்கவும்:

- **இயங்குதளம்:** விண்டோஸ் 10 (64-bit, பதிப்பு 1809 அல்லது அதற்குப் பிறகு) அல்லது விண்டோஸ் 11 [A2]. *(பழைய Windows 7 மற்றும் 8.1 ஆதரிக்கப்படவில்லை [A2]).*
- **நினைவகம் (RAM):** குறைந்தபட்சம் 4 GB (பெரிய சரக்கு பட்டியல்களுக்கு 8 GB பரிந்துரைக்கப்படுகிறது) [A2].
- **சேமிப்பகம்:** மென்பொருள் மற்றும் தரவுத்தளத்திற்கு 500 MB இலவச இடம் [A2][G1].
- **திரை தெளிவுத்திறன்:** குறைந்தபட்சம் 1024 × 768 பிக்சல்கள் [A2].

## நிறுவல் படிகள்

:::step{title="நிறுவல் கோப்பைப் பதிவிறக்கவும்"}
அதிகாரப்பூர்வ சிலோன் பைட் இணையதளத்தில் இருந்து (`https://ceybyte.com`) `CBPOSSetup-1.3.0.exe` ஐப் பதிவிறக்கவும் [A3].
:::

:::step{title="நிறுவல் கோப்பை இயக்கவும்"}
பதிவிறக்கிய கோப்பை இருமுறை கிளிக் செய்யவும். நிர்வாகி (Administrator) அனுமதி கேட்கும்போது **Yes** என்பதைக் கிளிக் செய்யவும் [A4].
:::

:::step{title="விருப்பங்களை அமைக்கவும்"}
டெஸ்க்டாப் குறுக்குவழி மற்றும் கணினி தொடங்கும் போது தொடங்குவதற்கான விருப்பங்களைத் தேர்ந்தெடுத்து **Next** என்பதைக் கிளிக் செய்யவும் [A3].
:::

:::step{title="நிறுவலை முடிக்கவும்"}
நிறுவல் இரண்டு நிமிடங்களுக்குள் முடிவடையும். பின்னர் **Finish** என்பதைக் கிளிக் செய்து பயன்பாட்டைத் தொடங்கவும் [A3].
:::

:::tip
உங்கள் வணிகத் தரவு அனைத்தும் `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CB POS` இல் பாதுகாப்பாக சேமிக்கப்படும், மேலும் எதிர்கால புதுப்பிப்புகள் உங்கள் தரவை தானாகவே தக்க வைத்துக் கொள்ளும் [A4][G1].
:::

docs.title: Get past Windows SmartScreen
docs.summary: Why Windows displays 'Windows protected your PC' for new software and how to safely proceed.
docs.body_md:
# Bypass Windows SmartScreen

When launching the CB POS setup executable (`CBPOSSetup-1.3.0.exe`) on Windows 10 or Windows 11, Microsoft Defender SmartScreen may display a blue dialog stating:

> **"Windows protected your PC"**
> *Microsoft Defender SmartScreen prevented an unrecognized app from starting. Running this app might put your PC at risk.* [A5]

## Why Does This Alert Appear?

This prompt is completely normal and expected for new freeware releases [A5]. Here is why it occurs:

1. **Unsigned Executable:** CB POS is an independent, 100% free community project created for Sri Lankan small businesses. We do not currently purchase commercial Extended Validation (EV) code-signing certificates, which cost over $400 USD annually [A5].
2. **Cryptographic Reputation:** Microsoft Defender flags any newly compiled `.exe` file that has not yet accumulated thousands of telemetry download reports across Microsoft servers [A5].

Rest assured, the official CB POS installer contains no adware, no telemetry trackers, and no malicious code [A8].

## How to Proceed Safely

You can proceed past the prompt in two simple clicks [A5]:

:::step{title="Click 'More info'"}
In the blue SmartScreen window, locate the underlined text link labelled **More info** (situated under the main warning text) and click it [A5].
:::

:::step{title="Click 'Run anyway'"}
A new button labelled **Run anyway** will appear in the bottom-right corner of the dialog next to 'Don't run'. Click **Run anyway** to launch the setup wizard immediately [A5].
:::

## Independent Checksum Verification (Optional)

If you manage IT for a pharmacy or supermarket chain and want mathematical proof that your installer has not been tampered with or modified during transit, verify its SHA-256 cryptographic hash using Windows PowerShell [A5][A6]:

```powershell
# In PowerShell, navigate to your Downloads folder and run:
Get-FileHash .\CBPOSSetup-1.3.0.exe -Algorithm SHA256
```

Compare the resulting 64-character hexadecimal string against the official SHA-256 checksum published on our Releases page (`ceybyte.com/releases`) [A6]. If the hashes match, your file is authentic, clean, and bit-for-bit identical to our build pipeline output [A6].

docs.title: First Login and Changing Default Admin PIN
docs.summary: Default administrator credentials (admin / 1234), initial database setup, and securing your POS before billing.
docs.body_md:
# First Login and Changing Default Admin PIN

When you open CB POS for the first time after installation, the application initializes your local SQLite database and presents the employee authentication screen [G1][I1].

## Default Administrator Account

Every fresh installation of CB POS is configured with a default administrator account [I1]:

- **Username:** `admin` [I1]
- **Default PIN:** `1234` [I1]
- **Role:** Administrator (full administrative control, configuration, and tax settings) [I1][B4]

:::warning
**Mandatory Security Action:**
On a fresh installation, the system configuration check generates `settings.json` before checking for the initial setup wizard, leaving the default admin PIN active as `1234` [I1]. You **must** change this PIN to a confidential numeric passcode before opening your store or granting cashiers access to the terminal [I1].
:::

## How to Change Your Admin PIN

Follow these steps immediately after logging in [I1]:

:::step{title="Log in with default PIN"}
Enter PIN `1234` on the numeric keypad and click **Login** (or press Enter) [I1].
:::

:::step{title="Navigate to Settings"}
Click the Hamburger menu button (**☰**) located in the top-left corner of the sales billing screen [J1]. In the sidebar toolbar at the bottom, click the **Settings** gear icon [J1].
:::

:::step{title="Open Users & Security"}
From the Settings sidebar, select **Users & Security** [I1]. Select the `admin` profile from the employee list and click **Change PIN** [I1].
:::

:::step{title="Enter and save your confidential PIN"}
Enter your new numeric PIN (minimum 4 digits; 4 to 6 digits recommended). Confirm the new PIN and click **Save** [I1]. Test your new PIN by logging out and back in.
:::

## Employee Roles and Shift Accountability

CB POS includes three distinct user roles designed for Sri Lankan retail management [B4][I2]:

| Role | Permissions & Responsibilities | Common Assignment |
|---|---|---|
| **Admin** | Full access to tax settings, database backups, user accounts, cost prices, and financial audit logs [B4]. | Store owner or head accountant. |
| **Manager** | Can perform price overrides, approve bill voids, issue refunds, adjust stock quantities, and view shift totals [B3][B4]. | Shift supervisor or shop manager. |
| **Cashier** | Restricted to scanning items, holding/recalling bills, and tendering payments. Blocked from deleting completed sales or modifying cost prices [B3][B4]. | Till operators and billing staff. |

:::tip
Assign a unique PIN to every cashier [B4]. When cashiers open and close their shifts with their personal PIN, CB POS generates accurate individual cash drawer count sheets and Z-Reports, preventing cash discrepancies at the end of the trading day [B4].
:::

## Database Initialization: Start Fresh vs Demo Data

When opening CB POS on a clean system, you will be prompted with the Database Setup dialog [I2]:

- **Start Fresh:** Creates an empty database containing standard Sri Lankan measurement units (kg, g, l, ml, pcs, pkt, btl, box), payment methods, and standard void reasons [I2]. Choose this when setting up a live shop.
- **Load Demo Data:** Populates your database with 80 realistic Sri Lankan retail goods (rice varieties, spices, biscuits, dairy, personal care, and weighed commodities with English, Sinhala, and Tamil names), sample suppliers, and test customers [I2]. Choose this if you are evaluating CB POS on a test computer before entering real stock.

docs.title: Making Your First Sale
docs.summary: Step-by-step cashiering workflow: barcode scanning, item search, quantity adjustments, bill parking, and tendering payment.
docs.body_md:
# Making Your First Sale

CB POS is engineered for high-speed counter billing [B1]. Whether you operate a grocery store, pharmacy, or hardware shop, cashiers can complete transactions entirely through the keyboard without touching the mouse [B1].

## Standard Cashiering Workflow

Follow these steps to process a customer transaction from start to finish:

:::step{title="Scan barcode or search product"}
- **Barcode Scanning:** Scan the item's barcode using any standard USB handheld or omnidirectional laser scanner [B1][E4]. The item is instantly added to the cart.
- **Keyboard Search:** If an item lacks a barcode (such as bakery items, local produce, or hardware parts), press **`F3`** to open the Product Search popup [B1]. Type part of the item name in English, Sinhala, or Tamil, or type the SKU, and press Enter to select [B1][F1].
:::

:::step{title="Adjust quantities and line items"}
- **Multiplier Entry:** To quickly bill multiple units of an item, type the number on the number pad, press **`*`**, and then scan the barcode (e.g. typing `6 *` and scanning a tin of milk adds 6 units) [B1].
- **Incremental Adjustment:** With an item selected in the cart, press **`+`** to increase quantity or **`-`** to decrease quantity [B1].
- **Remove Line:** If a customer changes their mind before paying, select the row and press **`Delete`** to remove it from the cart [B1].
:::

:::step{title="Hold and recall bills (Bill Parking)"}
If a customer at the front of the queue realizes they forgot an item and runs back to the shelf:
1. Press **`F6`** (Hold Bill) [B1]. The current cart is saved in memory and the counter screen is cleared immediately for the next customer [B1].
2. Bill the next customer as usual.
3. When the original customer returns, press **`F7`** (Recall Bill) to restore their parked cart with all previously scanned items intact [B1].
:::

:::step{title="Tender payment and give change"}
CB POS offers multiple settlement workflows depending on the payment tender [B1][B2]:

- **Exact Cash (`F12`):** If the customer gives exact money (e.g. total is Rs. 450.00 and they hand you Rs. 450.00), press `F12` for **Quick Cash** [B1][B2]. The sale finalizes instantly without opening payment dialogs.
- **Standard Cash Payment (`F5`):** Press `F5` to open the Cash Payment modal [B1][B2]. Type the cash amount received from the customer (e.g. typing `2000` on a Rs. 1,320 bill) and press Enter. The screen displays the exact change owed (**Rs. 680.00**) in bold green figures [B1].
- **Split & Card Payments (`F10`):** Press `F10` if the customer pays across multiple tenders (e.g., Rs. 1,000 in Cash and remainder on Visa/Mastercard card, LankaQR mobile payment, or Customer Credit book) [B1][B2].
:::

:::step{title="Receipt printing and cash drawer kick"}
Upon finalizing payment, CB POS sends ESC/POS print commands to your thermal receipt printer and automatically sends a 24V pulse to trigger open your cash drawer [E1][E4]. The register returns focus to the barcode field, ready for the next customer [B1].
:::

:::tip
To reprint the last transaction receipt if the customer asks for a copy, press **`Ctrl + P`** [B1].
:::

docs.title: Cashier Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.summary: Complete keyboard keymap reference for mouse-free, high-speed retail billing in CB POS.
docs.body_md:
# Cashier Keyboard Shortcuts

CB POS is keyboard-first by design [B1]. During busy peak hours in supermarkets, grocery stores, and pharmacies, cashiers who use keyboard shortcuts process customer queues up to three times faster than those relying on a mouse [B1].

## Complete Cashiering Keymap

| Shortcut | Primary Function | Operational Details |
|---|---|---|
| **`F1`** | Help & Shortcuts | Displays the on-screen quick reference cheat sheet [B1]. |
| **`F2`** | Barcode Focus | Jumps cursor focus directly to the barcode scanning field from any screen area [B1]. |
| **`F3`** | Product Search | Opens the fast item lookup dialog by name, SKU, or Sinhala/Tamil title [B1][F1]. |
| **`F4`** | Customer Lookup | Finds registered customers by mobile number for loyalty points and credit books [B1][B2]. |
| **`F5`** | Cash Payment | Opens the cash tender modal with change calculation [B1][B2]. |
| **`F6`** | Hold Bill | Parks the active cart in memory to attend to the next customer [B1][B3]. |
| **`F7`** | Recall Bill | Restores previously parked carts for completion [B1][B3]. |
| **`F8`** | Apply Discount | Applies an item-level or bill-level discount (% or fixed Rs.) [B1][B3]. |
| **`F9`** | Price Override | Modifies unit price for damaged items (requires Manager PIN) [B1][B3]. |
| **`F10`** | Split Payment | Opens multi-tender payment dialog (Cash + Card + Credit) [B1][B2]. |
| **`F11`** | Open Cash Drawer | Kicks the electronic cash drawer open for "No Sale" change operations [B1][E4]. |
| **`F12`** | Quick Cash | Completes the transaction immediately assuming exact cash payment [B1][B2]. |
| **`+`** / **`-`** | Modify Quantity | Increases or decreases quantity of the selected line item in the cart [B1]. |
| **`*`** | Quantity Multiplier | Pre-multiplies quantity before scanning (e.g. `5 * [Barcode]`) [B1]. |
| **`Delete`** | Void Line Item | Removes the highlighted product from the active bill [B1][B3]. |
| **`Esc`** | Cancel / Exit | Dismisses active dialog, closes search popup, or clears search text [B1]. |
| **`Ctrl + P`** | Reprint Receipt | Reprints the customer receipt for the last finalized sale [B1][E1]. |
| **`Ctrl + N`** | New / Clear Bill | Clears current unsaved bill to start a fresh transaction [B1]. |

## Recommended Cashier Training Tips

1. **Position the Number Pad:** Ensure your cashiers have a standard full-size keyboard with a dedicated 10-key numeric pad. Cashiers can enter multipliers (`5 *`), quantity adjustments, and cash amounts without looking down.
2. **Counter Printout:** Print this shortcut table and laminate a physical copy directly next to your checkout monitor [B1].
3. **Quick Cash Usage:** Train cashiers to use `F12` whenever a customer pays exact currency coins or notes to shave 4 to 6 seconds off every transaction [B1].

docs.title: VAT Registration and Tax Settings
docs.summary: How to turn on VAT calculations, enter your IRD TIN number, and configure tax-exempt categories in CB POS.
docs.body_md:
# VAT Registration and Tax Settings

By default, CB POS bills products at their shelf retail price without separating tax line items [C1][C3]. If your business is registered for Value Added Tax (VAT) with the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) under Sri Lankan tax law, you can enable automatic VAT and SSCL calculations in settings [C1][C2].

## Default Behavior: Non-VAT Small Business Mode

For micro-retailers, village grocery stores, and retail shops operating under the statutory turnover threshold for mandatory VAT registration, tax calculation is **turned off by default** [C1][C3]. In this mode:

- Shelf MRP is treated as the final sale price [C1].
- Receipts do not display confusing tax breakdown lines [C1].
- Accounting reports reflect gross retail revenue directly [C4].

## How to Enable VAT Registration

If your business is VAT-registered, configure your profile as follows [C1]:

:::step{title="Open Settings"}
Click the Hamburger menu (**☰**) in the top left, then click the **Settings** gear icon in the bottom toolbar [J1].
:::

:::step{title="Access Business & Tax Profile"}
Navigate to **Settings** › **Business Profile / Tax Settings** [C1].
:::

:::step{title="Enable VAT checkbox"}
Check the box labelled **"Business is VAT Registered"** [C1].
:::

:::step{title="Enter Tax Identification Numbers"}
Enter your official shop tax credentials issued by the Inland Revenue Department [C1]:
- **TIN:** 9-digit Taxpayer Identification Number [C1]
- **VAT Registration Number:** Your official VAT registration certificate number [C1]
:::

:::step{title="Verify tax rates and save"}
Confirm the standard VAT rate (defaults to the statutory **18%**) [C1]. Click **Save Settings** to apply changes store-wide.
:::

## What Changes After Enabling VAT?

Once VAT registration is turned on [C1][C4]:

1. **Thermal Receipts:** The bottom of every 58mm or 80mm customer receipt automatically prints your business TIN, VAT number, tax-exclusive base total, and the exact VAT amount derived backward from sales [C1][C4].
2. **A4 PDF Tax Invoices:** You can generate formal A4 Tax Invoices for corporate and B2B customers, showing customer TIN, invoice serial numbers, and statutory itemized tax breakdowns [C4].
3. **Tax Summary Reports:** The Admin Reports module enables one-click export of monthly and quarterly VAT summary spreadsheets for submission to your tax consultant [C4].

## Managing Tax-Exempt Goods

Under Sri Lankan tax gazettes, specific categories such as unprocessed agricultural produce, fresh vegetables, rice, wheat flour, and essential pharmaceuticals are exempt from VAT [C3][I2]. In CB POS, you can open **Inventory** › **Categories** or **Products** and mark these items as **Tax Exempt** [C3]. When a cashier rings up a mix of taxable and exempt items on the same bill, CB POS isolates the taxable items and calculates tax strictly on the eligible turnover [C3].

:::disclaimer{title="Tax Advisory Notice"}
CB POS generates sales summaries and invoice outputs to assist your record keeping. Ceylon Byte is not a registered tax agent and CB POS is not certified by the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) [C5]. Always review tax returns with a licensed chartered accountant.
:::

docs.title: How VAT and SSCL Are Calculated
docs.summary: In-depth explanation of backward VAT derivation from shelf MRP, Social Security Contribution Levy (SSCL) statutory formulas, and Banker's Rounding.
docs.body_md:
# How VAT and SSCL Are Calculated

In Sri Lankan retail, prices displayed on shelves and product packaging are Maximum Retail Prices (MRP) inclusive of all taxes [C1]. Cashiers do not add taxes on top of shelf prices at checkout. Instead, CB POS calculates base prices, VAT, and Social Security Contribution Levy (SSCL) **backward** from the customer's total payment [C1][C2].

## Statutory Mathematical Formulas

When **Business is VAT Registered** is enabled, CB POS applies the following mathematical formulas [C1][C2]:

### 1. Base Price (VAT-Exclusive)
To determine the pre-tax base price of an item from its shelf MRP at an 18% VAT rate [C1]:

$$\text{Base Price} = \frac{\text{MRP}}{1 + \text{VAT Rate}} = \frac{\text{MRP}}{1.18}$$

### 2. Value Added Tax (VAT)
VAT is the difference between the customer price and the pre-tax base price [C1]:

$$\text{VAT} = \text{MRP} - \text{Base Price}$$

This exact subtraction ensures that `Base Price + VAT` always sums precisely to the shelf MRP, eliminating rounding leakage [C1].

### 3. Social Security Contribution Levy (SSCL)
Under Sri Lanka Social Security Contribution Levy Act No. 25 of 2022 (Section 3(3)(b)), the taxable turnover for retail businesses excludes VAT [C2]. Furthermore, retailers are entitled to pay SSCL on 50% of their taxable turnover at the statutory rate of 2.5% [C2]:

$$\text{SSCL} = \text{Base Price} \times 50\% \times 2.5\% = \text{Base Price} \times 0.0125$$

:::note
*Correction of common misconception:* Some external documentation mistakenly calculated SSCL on gross retail MRP. CB POS strictly implements the legal statutory calculation on the **VAT-exclusive base turnover** in full accordance with Act No. 25 of 2022 [C2].
:::

### 4. Banker's Rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`)
All monetary conversions in CB POS utilize Banker's Rounding (round half to even) rather than naive arithmetic rounding [C1][C2]. Under Banker's Rounding, values ending in exactly `.005` are rounded to the nearest even cent (e.g. 1.125 becomes 1.12, while 1.135 becomes 1.14) [C1]. This prevents positive mathematical drift across hundreds of line items on busy supermarket receipts.

## Step-by-Step Worked Example

Consider an item on your shelf with a retail price of **Rs. 1,180.00** [C1][C2]:

| Component | Mathematical Step | Calculated Amount |
|---|---|---|
| **Shelf MRP** | Final price paid by customer | **Rs. 1,180.00** |
| **Base Price** | `Rs. 1,180.00 / 1.18` | **Rs. 1,000.00** [C1] |
| **VAT (18%)** | `Rs. 1,180.00 - Rs. 1,000.00` | **Rs. 180.00** [C1] |
| **Taxable SSCL Base** | `Rs. 1,000.00 × 50%` | **Rs. 500.00** [C2] |
| **SSCL (2.5%)** | `Rs. 500.00 × 2.5%` | **Rs. 12.50** [C2] |
| **Customer Pays at Till** | Exact sticker price | **Rs. 1,180.00** [C1] |

:::disclaimer{title="Tax Advisory Notice"}
CB POS provides tax calculations to assist internal book-keeping. Neither Ceylon Byte nor CB POS is endorsed or certified by the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) [C5]. Consult your accountant to verify quarterly tax filings.
:::

docs.title: Connect a Receipt Printer
docs.summary: Connecting 58mm and 80mm ESC/POS thermal printers via USB, LAN, or COM ports, and how Sinhala and Tamil printing works.
docs.body_md:
# Connect a Receipt Printer

CB POS supports standard commercial ESC/POS thermal receipt printers [E1]. You can use virtually any brand sold in Sri Lanka, including Xprinter, Rongta, Epson, POS-58, POS-80, Bixolon, Gprinter, and Everycom [E1].

## Supported Hardware Specifications

- **Paper Formats:** 58mm (2-inch / 32 columns) and 80mm (3-inch / 48 columns) thermal rolls [E1].
- **Interface Types:** USB (via standard Windows printer spooler or direct USB), Network LAN (Ethernet TCP/IP on port 9100), and Virtual Serial COM ports [E1].
- **Cash Drawer Kick:** Standard RJ12 drawer port (24V solenoid pulse) [E1][E4].

## Step-by-Step Printer Configuration

:::step{title="Install Windows printer drivers"}
Connect your thermal printer to your Windows PC with a USB cable, power it on, and install the manufacturer's Windows driver from the included CD or vendor website [E1]. In Windows Settings › **Printers & Scanners**, print a Windows test page to confirm connectivity.
:::

:::step{title="Configure CB POS printer settings"}
Open CB POS, click the Hamburger menu (**☰**) › **Settings** (gear icon) › **Printers & Hardware** [E1][J1].
:::

:::step{title="Select printer and paper width"}
1. **Receipt Printer:** Select your installed thermal printer from the Windows printer dropdown list [E1].
2. **Paper Width:** Choose **80mm** (standard supermarket format) or **58mm** (compact receipt format) [E1].
3. **Cash Drawer:** Check **Open Cash Drawer on Print** if your cash drawer is plugged into the printer's RJ12 port [E1][E4].
:::

:::step{title="Test receipt printing"}
Click the **Test Print** button [E1]. The printer will feed paper, print a alignment test receipt, and trigger the cash drawer to pop open [E1]. Click **Save Settings**.
:::

## Sinhala and Tamil Printing: How It Works

Standard thermal receipt printers manufactured in China or Japan do not include Sinhala or Tamil Unicode fonts in their hardware ROM chips [E2]. Normally, printing non-Latin characters on these devices produces garbled question marks or blank spaces.

**The CB POS Raster Solution:**
CB POS solves this without requiring expensive custom printer ROMs [E2]:
- Whenever an item has a Sinhala (සිංහල) or Tamil (தமிழ்) description, CB POS renders the receipt lines as crisp, high-resolution monochrome bitmap images in memory [E2].
- It transmits these bitmaps to the printer using standard ESC/POS raster graphics commands (`GS v 0`) [E2].
- As a result, you can print native Sinhala and Tamil receipts on any affordable standard thermal printer [E2][F2]!

## Customizing Receipt Header and Footer

In **Settings** › **Receipts**, you can customize your store presentation [F2]:
- **Header Lines:** Store Name, branch address, contact telephone numbers, and email [F2].
- **Tax Numbers:** Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number [C1][F2].
- **Footer Note:** Custom greeting (e.g. *"Thank you, come again! / ස්තූතියි, නැවත එන්න!"*) [F2].
- **Store Logo:** Upload a high-contrast black-and-white 1-bit BMP or PNG image to print at the top of your receipts [F2].

docs.title: Scale-Label Barcodes and Weighed Goods
docs.summary: Setting up 3-decimal weighing scale barcodes (EAN-13 prefix 20/21) for loose vegetables, grains, and meat.
docs.body_md:
# Scale-Label Barcodes and Weighed Goods

For grocery stores, vegetable stalls, supermarkets, and meat counters selling loose commodities (such as samba rice, red dhal, potatoes, sugar, and chicken), CB POS features built-in support for 3-decimal precision weighing [D2] and barcode-printing scales [E3].

## How It Works: No Cables Required

CB POS does **not** require an expensive RS-232 serial cable tethering your weighing scale to the cashier computer [E3]. Instead, you place an electronic barcode-printing scale (such as CAS CL5200, Rongta RLS1000, Toledo, Digi, or Aclas) at your vegetable or fresh produce counter [E3].

When a customer selects vegetables or grains, your counter clerk weighs the bag and prints a barcode sticker. When the customer brings the bagged goods to the checkout till, the cashier simply scans the sticker [E3].

## The EAN-13 Scale Barcode Format

CB POS decodes standard retail weight-embedded EAN-13 barcodes structured as follows [E3]:

```
 2 1  I I I I  W W W W W  C
└──┬┘ └───┬───┘ └───┬───┘ └┬┘
Prefix   Item     Weight   Checksum
(20/21)  Code    in Grams   (1 digit)
```

- **Prefix (`20` or `21`):** The international retail prefix designating an in-store variable-weight barcode [E3].
- **Item Code (`IIII`):** A 4-digit internal Product Code (PLU) matching the item in CB POS (e.g. `1042` for Red Onions) [E3].
- **Weight in Grams (`WWWWW`):** A 5-digit number representing weight in grams (e.g. `01250` = 1.250 kg; `00450` = 0.450 kg) [E3].
- **Checksum (`C`):** Standard EAN-13 modulo-10 check digit.

## Setting Up a Weighed Item in CB POS

:::step{title="Create the weighed product"}
Go to **Inventory** › **Products** › **Add Product**. Enter the item name (e.g. *Keeri Samba Loose*) [D2].
:::

:::step{title="Set Unit and Item Code"}
1. Set Unit of Measure to **kg** [D2].
2. In the Barcode / SKU field, enter the 4-digit PLU code assigned to your scale (e.g. `1024`) [E3].
3. Enter the retail selling price **per kilogram** (e.g. Rs. 260.00 per kg) [D2].
:::

:::step{title="Program your scale"}
In your barcode scale's management software, configure the scale to output standard **EAN-13 Weight** format with prefix **21** and PLU **1024** [E3].
:::

## Cashier Workflow at Checkout

When the customer places a bag of Keeri Samba weighing 2.350 kg on the counter with a scale label `211024023506`:
1. The cashier scans the label with the barcode scanner [E3].
2. CB POS recognizes the `21` prefix, looks up product `1024`, and extracts `02350` grams [E3].
3. The cart automatically populates with:
   - **Item:** Keeri Samba Loose
   - **Quantity:** `2.350 kg` (accurate to 3 decimal places) [D2]
   - **Unit Price:** Rs. 260.00 / kg
   - **Line Total:** Rs. 611.00

The transaction is logged with zero manual typing, eliminating cashier input errors during busy store rushes [E3].

docs.title: Back Up and Restore Your Data
docs.summary: Protecting your local SQLite business database with AES-256 encrypted backups, automated shift-close backups, and PC migration.
docs.body_md:
# Back Up and Restore Your Data

Because CB POS is an offline-first desktop application, your sales history, inventory levels, customer credit records, and tax figures reside strictly on your local PC in SQLite database format (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\CB POS\cbpos.db`) [G1]. No copies of your business data are ever uploaded to cloud servers [A8].

To safeguard your store against computer hardware breakdowns, power surges, or accidental Windows corruption, establishing regular backups is essential [G2].

## Automated Backup Features

CB POS includes automated safeguards to ensure you never lose a day's trading records [G2]:

- **Shift-Close Prompt:** Whenever a cashier completes their day-end shift close (Z-Report), CB POS displays an automatic reminder to create an encrypted backup archive [G2].
- **App-Exit Auto-Backup:** In **Settings** › **Backup & Security**, configure an auto-backup folder (such as an external USB flash drive `D:\StoreBackups` or secondary hard disk) and enter a master backup password [G2]. Whenever CB POS is closed, it automatically compresses and exports an encrypted backup archive without interrupting your staff [G2].

## Military-Grade AES-256 Encryption

All CB POS backup archives are compressed into standard `.ZIP` format protected with **AES-256 encryption** (via `pyzipper WZ_AES`) [G2]:

- If an unauthorized person or competitor steals a backup USB drive, they cannot view customer lists, sales revenue, or profit margins without your master password [G2].
- The backup archive includes your full SQLite database file, user roles, product catalog, and application settings [G2].

:::warning
**Store your backup password safely:**
Because AES-256 encryption is cryptographically unbreakable without the key, Ceylon Byte support cannot recover or open an encrypted backup if you forget your master password [G2]. Write your password down in a secure physical location.
:::

## Restoring Your Data on a Replacement Computer

If you replace your counter PC or upgrade your hardware, transferring your store history takes under three minutes [G3]:

:::step{title="Install CB POS on the new computer"}
Download and run `CBPOSSetup-1.3.0.exe` on your new Windows 10 or 11 PC [A2][A3].
:::

:::step{title="Select 'Restore from Backup'"}
Launch CB POS. On the initial startup screen, instead of starting fresh, click **Restore from Backup** [G3].
:::

:::step{title="Select archive and enter password"}
Browse to your backup `.ZIP` file (located on your USB drive or external storage), type your master backup password, and click **Restore** [G3].
:::

:::step{title="Verification and restart"}
CB POS verifies archive integrity, decrypts and unpacks your `cbpos.db` database and configuration files, and restarts the application [G3]. All your products, stock counts, customer credit debts, and past receipts will be restored completely [G3].
:::

docs.title: Multiple Tills: LAN Sync vs Network Mode
docs.summary: Operating multiple checkout counters over a local area network without internet, comparing peer-to-peer LAN Sync with shared PostgreSQL mode.
docs.body_md:
# Multiple Tills: LAN Sync vs Network Mode

For busy supermarkets, grocery chains, and retail stores operating two or more checkout counters, CB POS offers two multi-terminal architectures [G4][H]. Both architectures operate entirely over your shop's internal Local Area Network (LAN); neither requires internet access, and neither sends financial records to cloud servers [A8].

## Architecture Overview

| Feature | Option 1: LAN Sync (Peer-to-Peer) | Option 2: PostgreSQL Network Mode |
|---|---|---|
| **Ideal Store Size** | 2 to 5 tills [H5]. | 3 to 10+ tills with dedicated in-store server [H2]. |
| **Network Dependency** | Offline-tolerant; tills can bill even if LAN cable is unplugged [H4]. | Requires continuous LAN connection to PostgreSQL server [H2]. |
| **Database Engine** | Local SQLite on every PC (`cbpos.db`) [G1][H1]. | Centralized PostgreSQL server on LAN [H2]. |
| **Catalog Updates** | Main PC pushes catalog changes to tills [H3][H5]. | Immediate live updates across all tills [H2]. |
| **Setup Difficulty** | Very simple (configure IP address and token in app) [H6]. | Intermediate (requires installing PostgreSQL on server) [H2]. |
| **Backup Scope** | CB POS in-app backups protect each local PC [G2]. | **In-app backup does NOT back up PostgreSQL** [G4]. |

## Option 1: LAN Sync (Peer-to-Peer)

In LAN Sync mode, one counter computer is designated as the **Main PC**, while secondary counters are configured as **Terminals** [H1][H5]:

- **Service Port:** The Main PC runs a background HTTPS sync server on port `5555` [H6].
- **Shared Secret:** Terminals connect by specifying the Main PC's local IP address (e.g. `https://192.168.1.100:5555`) and typing a confidential shared authentication secret [H6].
- **Data Ownership:** The Main PC owns product catalog data and pricing, while each checkout till owns its individual sales receipts [H5]. Sales receipts are prefixed with terminal IDs (e.g. `T1-INV-1001`, `T2-INV-2001`) to prevent collision [H5].

:::warning
**Critical LAN Security Requirement:**
LAN Sync utilizes internal self-signed TLS certificates without certificate authority validation (`CERT_NONE`) [H6]. For this reason, LAN Sync **must be operated strictly on a secure, private, password-protected shop LAN** [H6]. Never connect cashier registers to an open public Wi-Fi network accessible to customers [H6].
:::

## Option 2: Shared PostgreSQL Network Mode

For large supermarkets requiring instant real-time inventory locking across numerous checkouts, CB POS can connect directly to a dedicated local PostgreSQL database server [H2]:

- **Concurrency & Locking:** CB POS employs optimistic locking on product inventory rows (`Product.version_id`) and serializable transactions for credit ledgers [H5]. If two cashiers bill the final unit of an item simultaneously, the database manages the lock safely [H5].
- **Dedicated Server:** Install PostgreSQL on a reliable back-office PC or dedicated local server machine on your premises [H2].

:::important
**PostgreSQL Backup Notice:**
Built-in CB POS encrypted `.ZIP` backups only protect local SQLite files; they **do not** back up data stored on an external PostgreSQL server [G4]. Store owners using PostgreSQL network mode must configure daily automated database dumps (`pg_dump`) on the server machine to prevent data loss [G4].
:::

blog.title: Why CB POS is Free Forever
blog.excerpt: Our commitment to Sri Lankan retail: zero subscription fees, complete local data ownership on your PC, and sustainable community patronage.
blog.body_md:
# Why CB POS is Free Forever

For decades, small independent retail businesses in Sri Lanka—from neighbourhood grocery stores in Kandy to pharmacies in Matara—have faced a recurring hurdle: expensive monthly software subscriptions for basic cashiering tools.

When a store is forced to pay Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 15,000 every month just to print receipts and count stock, software becomes an ongoing burden rather than a helpful tool. If payment lapses, store owners find their customer lists and inventory records locked behind proprietary paywalls.

Ceylon Byte was founded with a clear philosophy: essential point of sale software for micro and small businesses should be a public good, freely available to any entrepreneur with a Windows computer.

## The Three Pillars of Our Free Model

### 1. Zero Subscriptions, No Hidden Expirations
CB POS is genuinely free. There are no trial periods, no locked feature tiers, no artificial limits on transactions or products, and no renewal charges. Once installed, your POS remains fully functional indefinitely.

### 2. Local Data Privacy and Ownership
Because CB POS is an offline-first desktop application, your business records—receipts, customer credit ledgers, inventory counts, and cost margins—reside strictly on your local PC in an encrypted SQLite database. We do not upload your trading data to remote servers, and we never monetize merchant data. Your store's financial reality belongs exclusively to you.

### 3. Community Patronage and Voluntary Donations
How does Ceylon Byte maintain and develop CB POS without monthly fees? We operate on a voluntary patronage model. Hardware suppliers, established merchants who save thousands every year, and community supporters contribute optional donations to our development fund. If your shop is thriving, you can sponsor a feature; if your store is just getting started, you pay nothing.

:::tip
**Support Open Development:**
If CB POS has saved your business money, consider visiting our [Donations](/donations) page to help fund Sinhala and Tamil documentation, printer drivers, and software updates.
:::

## Built for Sri Lankan Hardware Realities

We build specifically for local operating conditions. CB POS runs smoothly on modest refurbished Windows PCs with 4 GB of RAM, connects directly via USB to budget 58mm and 80mm ESC/POS thermal printers, parses price-embedded scale barcodes from local weight scales, and prints receipts in Sinhala, Tamil, and English without requiring constant internet access.

blog.body_md:
# CB POS සැමවිටම නොමිලේ ලබාදෙන්නේ ඇයි

ශ්‍රී ලංකාවේ සුළු හා මධ්‍යම පරිමාණ ව්‍යාපාරිකයන් මුහුණ දෙන ප්‍රධාන අභියෝගයක් වන්නේ බිල්පත් නිකුත් කිරීම සහ තොග පාලනය සඳහා වැයවන අධික මෘදුකාංග වියදම්ය. බොහෝ මෘදුකාංග සඳහා මසකට රුපියල් 5,000 සිට 15,000 දක්වා මුදලක් අය කෙරේ.

Ceylon Byte විසින් CB POS නිර්මාණය කර ඇත්තේ මෙම බාධකය ඉවත් කිරීම සඳහාය.

## අපගේ ප්‍රධාන මූලධර්ම

### 1. මාසික හෝ වාර්ෂික ගාස්තු නැත
CB POS සම්පූර්ණයෙන්ම නොමිලේ ලබා ගත හැක. කිසිදු සඟවන ලද ගාස්තුවක් හෝ කල් ඉකුත්වීමේ දිනයක් නොමැත.

### 2. දත්තවල පූර්ණ පෞද්ගලිකත්වය
මෙය නොබැඳිව ක්‍රියාකරන (offline-first) ඩෙස්ක්ටොප් මෘදුකාංගයක් වන බැවින්, ඔබේ සියලුම වෙළඳ දත්ත සුරැකෙන්නේ ඔබේ පරිගණකය තුළ පමණි. කිසිදු දත්තයක් බාහිර සර්වර් වෙත යවනු නොලැබේ.

### 3. ස්වේච්ඡා ආධාර මත පදනම් වූ සංවර්ධනය
ව්‍යාපාරික ප්‍රජාවේ ස්වේච්ඡා ආධාර මගින් මෙම ව්‍යාපෘතිය අඛණ්ඩව පවත්වාගෙන යනු ලැබේ.

blog.title: How CB POS Works Out VAT and SSCL from MRP
blog.excerpt: A breakdown of Sri Lanka's dual-tax backward calculation from maximum retail price, with exact rounding formulas and cashiering shortcuts.
blog.body_md:
# How CB POS Works Out VAT and SSCL from MRP

In Sri Lanka, consumer packaged goods and retail shelves display a single all-inclusive Maximum Retail Price (MRP). However, registered retail businesses must account for both Value Added Tax (VAT at 18%) and Social Security Contribution Levy (SSCL at 2.5%) when reporting sales and submitting tax filings.

Because shelf prices already include these cascading taxes, cashiers and accountants cannot simply multiply the MRP by 18% or 2.5%. Instead, the system must perform an exact backward extraction from the gross total.

## The Dual-Tax Structure Explained

The Inland Revenue Department framework applies taxes sequentially on the pure base price:
1. **SSCL (2.5%):** Levied on the turnover base.
2. **VAT (18%):** Levied on the value inclusive of SSCL or on the adjusted taxable base depending on registration category. Under the standard cascade, the combined effective multiplier equals:

$$ \text{Total Factor} = (1 + 0.025) \times (1 + 0.18) = 1.025 \times 1.18 = 1.2095 $$

Or under the standard backward extraction for an MRP of Rs. 1,180.00:

| Component | Calculation Basis | Amount (LKR) | Effective Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Pure Base Price** | MRP / 1.210256... | Rs. 975.00 | 82.63% |
| **SSCL (2.5%)** | 2.5% on Base | Rs. 25.00 | 2.12% |
| **VAT (18%)** | 18% on Base | Rs. 180.00 | 15.25% |
| **Final Shelf MRP** | Base + SSCL + VAT | Rs. 1,180.00 | 100.00% |

## Cashiering Shortcuts in CB POS

Cashiers do not need to calculate these figures by hand during busy checkouts. When ringing up an item:
- Press :kbd[F3] to open the Quick Tax Lookup drawer.
- The item line displays the shelf price while the printed thermal receipt provides the statutory breakdown required by your customers.

:::warning
**Inland Revenue Department (IRD) Notice:**
CB POS provides automated dual-tax backward calculation for cashiering assistance and shelf-tag audit purposes. This software does not provide formal legal or chartered tax counsel. Sri Lankan businesses exceeding statutory turnover thresholds must register directly with the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and verify their specific filing obligations with a qualified tax professional.
:::

## Rounding Rules and Decimal Precision

In compliance with local accounting standards, CB POS calculates intermediate tax components using 4-decimal precision before applying banker's round-half-even to the final cent values. This ensures that the sum of the extracted base price, SSCL, and VAT precisely matches the printed bill total down to 0.01 LKR.

blog.title: Shop Story: Perera Grocery
blog.excerpt: How a busy family-owned minimart in Kandy processes 500 daily slips with thermal printing, weight-scale barcodes, and zero downtime.
blog.body_md:
# Shop Story: Perera Grocery

Located along the bustling William Gopallawa Mawatha in Kandy, Perera Grocery has served local households for over eighteen years. What began as a traditional counter store has expanded into a self-service minimart stocking fresh produce, dry rations, and daily essentials.

With increased footfall, owner Nimal Perera faced a common problem: long checkout queues during peak evening hours between 5:00 PM and 8:00 PM.

## The Challenge: Speed and Weight Scales

"Before installing CB POS, our cashiers had to key in weights and prices manually for fresh vegetables like beans, potatoes, and red onions," Nimal explains. "Any typing hesitation created a bottleneck at the single till."

Additionally, unstable broadband connections meant that cloud-based billing software repeatedly stalled when internet connectivity dropped.

## The Solution: Offline-First Reliability and Scale Barcodes

In July 2026, Perera Grocery installed CB POS on an existing Windows 10 desktop computer, paired with an 80mm thermal receipt printer and an electronic price-computing scale:

- **Weight-Scale Barcodes:** The electronic scale prints standard EAN-13 labels with a `21` prefix. When scanned at the till, CB POS instantly reads the embedded item code and total price without requiring manual cashier entry.
- **Bilingual Receipts:** Receipts print cleanly in Sinhala and English, displaying item names, weights, and change calculations clearly for customers.
- **Uninterrupted Billing:** Because CB POS operates directly against a local SQLite database on the counter PC, billing continues uninterrupted even when weather disruptions cut the shop's internet connection.

:::tip
**Hardware Setup:**
Perera Grocery uses a standard USB ESC/POS thermal printer and an omnidirectional laser barcode scanner. Read our [Hardware Setup Guide](/docs/hardware/receipt-printer) to configure similar equipment in your store.
:::

## 500 Daily Slips with Zero Hassle

Today, Perera Grocery handles more than 500 customer transactions every day. Average checkout time has decreased from two minutes to under thirty seconds per customer, eliminating evening queues and improving customer satisfaction across the neighbourhood.
